Orbit view: 2x upscale of hero, unproject on fitted sphere, delight, far side painted at dive patch detail (tiles, poles on polar projection), hero pixels on the visible side faded toward the limb, light curve measured, fitted haze layers plus one across the disc edge, cloud band flow layer, night side lightning, hero sky as sky patch.

- 07:10 to 07:19 motion taps in the stop's own shader (`globe.ts`, `set.ts`, `look.ts motion`): in dive and rise frames of the orbit view with more than one sample, `set.ts` takes the plan's pose at the sample time and one sample interval later, measures how far nine surface points slide on screen (`slide`), and when that is over 1.25 px gives the globe shader `uTaps` (one per px, at most 12) and the next sample's camera in the mesh frame (`uCamObj`, `uNextCam`, `uNextRot`, with the change of lens). The shader finds where this pixel's ray meets the sphere now and one sample later and averages the wrap and patch reads along that path, centred on the sample. So the blur never grows past the shutter, it only fills the gaps between samples. Light, haze, limb and lightning are computed once.

### Item 2, the covers (10:40 onward)

- Cover engine facts: `src/terrain/cover.ts` draws its own horizon band (`uLow` below, `uColor` above), darkens above the horizon by `uTop` over 0.22 tan units, alpha from the amount (1 above 0.93), cut by the shell (distance of the ray from the planet centre). `film.ts` order per frame: `coverAmount`, `coverSide`, colours, `coverTop`, `horizon()`, `coverShell`. `coverSide` blends over the middle half of the 16 frame window (dive 0 to 1, rise 1 to 0).
- Diagnosis, rise (review cover sheet of 09:31): dark sky above the horizon 1555 to 1558, all cream 1559 to 1563, black sky from 1564: dark, bright, dark reads as a cut. Cause: `coverTop` 0.85 on the orbit side made the cover's own sky cream. The rise's horizon itself is carried (tilt 0 to 1564, height in frame 0.13 at 1559, 0.141 at 1560, rising smoothly).

- `npx tsx assets-src/venus/motion/horizon.ts` prints per frame around both covers: view, altitude, vfov, limb tilt, height in frame, cover amount, side, shell. After the override: tilt -88.0 (1288), -82.7 (1292), -72.3 (1296), -58.9 (1300), -44.6 (1304), -37.8 (1306), -28.8 (1309), -23.9 (1311), -20.3 (1313), -19.0 (1314, terrain), -14.6 (1318), -10.9 (1322), -6.4 (1328), -4.6 (1331), 0 at 1350: at most 3.5 degrees per frame, no stop. ### Item 5, cloud detail (10:45 onward)

- Orange blocks on the bright cumulus edges (seen at 1185 and 1287 in native crops, the hero is cream there). Cause measured: the wrap stores albedo up to `TOP` 24 and scales brighter texels down with their hue kept. The sunlit cumulus tops on the night side need up to 135 (hero scene value 4.97 clipped in red, light curve there 0.042, 0.071, 0.108): stored 24, 6, 0.6 for a true 125, 31, 3.3. Five times too dim in scene light, and under the tone curve that is orange where the hero is nearly white. Not a JPEG fault (all maps are 4:4:4).
- Fix: the missing factor is stored. `wrap/lift.py` writes log2(true peak / 24) / 3 into the green channel of `wrap-flow.jpg` (red stays the flow layer; 0.019 percent of the map lifted, median 1.9, all with cap weight over 0.42, so nothing of the hero's limb glow). `globe.ts`: `lin *= exp2(max(g - floor, 0) * 3 * smoothstep(0.4, 0.8, texel peak))` (`look.lift`). The gate on the texel's own brightness keeps the soft lift map from brightening dark cloud beside a highlight in the patches. No new texture, no more memory.
- Black single pixels on the limb line at 1287 (draft): the globe mesh is a polygon (320 segments), its silhouette lies up to 4.8e-5 radii inside the sphere, the rim shader discards exactly inside the sphere: a gap of up to 0.026 px at 540 px radius, so about 2.6 percent of limb samples saw the sky between the two. Fix: the mesh is drawn 1 / cos(pi / seg) + 2e-4 larger and the globe shader discards rays that miss the unit sphere (same test as the rim, at the end of main so derivatives stay defined). The "dotted dark line" seen at review at -70 and -20 degrees was this, not the sharpen.
- Thin orange arcs near the grazing limb (vortex side, also 1287 upper right): streaks of the generated map in the outer 9 px, foreshortened to one pixel and kept sharp by anisotropic filtering. Fix: `look.graze = { most: 4, from: 0.32, to: 0.06 }`: the texture footprint of the wrap and the patches grows by up to 5 times as the view angle cosine falls from 0.32 to 0.06, as thick haze would do.
- Lightning: the painted bolt texture was read with an implicit derivative inside a branch (undefined mip level). Now `textureGrad` with the derivatives of the plane coordinate.
- Rise 1586 "combed, embossed strokes": the flow layer is drawn as veil(now) / veil(hold middle). By the rise the two are 12 degrees apart, so the map's own streaks are cancelled and a displaced copy laid over them: a double pattern. Fix in `set.ts`: after the terrain view the flow layer's clock is counted from the judged rise frame (`look.drift.riseAt` 0.75 of the rise), so the veil is neutral at 1586 and drifts around it. The globe is hidden by the covers and the terrain view in between, so nothing jumps in view. The band drift (the map's own shear) is unchanged and continuous.
- Item 6, terrain: `terrain.forward` 0.6 to 1.2 (the judged frame 1440 is the middle of the move and does not change).
- 11:00 results of the test job (`out/work/venus/r2/t1-*.png`): cumulus tops cream at 1185 and 1287 (crops in looks), no black limb pixels at 1287 in that take, 1586 neutral veil. Pushed as fbbb040 with the binaries of round 2 so far. Engine batch 11 merged (fa0cb77): sample count follows screen motion.
- `terrain.forward` 1.2 showed the near edge of the relief as a flat brown strip along the bottom of 1350 (60 px), 0.95 still 10 px; 0.85 is clean at 1338, 1344, 1350 (`r2/f85-*.png`). So forward is 0.85 (was 0.6 in round 1). Share of texels under 1.0 in the terrain view stays 0.
- Where the 1.8 percent of mean level over the hero sits (review 1185): disc inside 400 px +0.6 percent, sky +3 percent (0.5 of 255), halo ring 456 to 560 px +6.4 percent. Edge by steepest slope: film 457 to 459 px all round, hero 454 to 455 at top and bottom and 458 to 462 left and right. The hero's disc is 0.8 percent flattened, the film's is round and 3 px larger at top and bottom, where the limb is brightest. Not chased (a flattened globe would break the analytic limb).
- Limb ring arcs, second pass. `look.graze = { most: 3, from: 0.45, to: 0.2 }` softened the arcs at the hold only a little, and at 1287 the red broken strokes sit further inside the limb (the dive camera sees the hero's limb ring less steeply). Cause in the map itself: `/tmp/limbzone.png` (the wrap relit in the hero's view, without haze) shows red streaks in the ring where the hero is a smooth golden band; taking the limb glow out of the hero and dividing by a light curve near zero left amplified streaks. Fix in the asset, `wrap/calm.py`: in the ring of hold view cosine -0.02 to 0.44 (weight 1 from 0.26 down) the stored value is pulled toward its local mean in log space (value = base * (value / base)^k, k down to 0.15, base = Gaussian of 1 degree). Applied to `wrap-color.jpg` and `patch-a.jpg` of both sets from the backups in `out/work/venus/r2/bak/` (19 percent of the wrap, 17 percent of patch a; patch b, c, d lie outside). Result: review 1185 against the hero in the ring 395 to 452 px 5.98 (before 6.15), whole frame 4.82 (4.83); the arcs are gone at 1185 and 1287 (`/tmp/vortex-crop6.png`, `/tmp/c1287-e.png`).
- Black limb pixels came back at draft 1287 in another take (one or two per frame): the globe and the rim each decide "inside the sphere" from their own interpolated ray, and the two differ in the last bits. Fix: the rim no longer decides. It is depth tested against the globe (back faces of its 2.6 radius shell, so always behind the globe; the orbit group holds nothing else that writes depth) and clamps b to at least 1. A pixel is the globe's or the rim's, never neither and never both.

## Phase 6 polish, item 1: the covers (19:50 onward)

Render copy and scripts as before (`/home/user/workspace/r2`). New: `sync2.sh eng|main` (eng puts the engine files of agent/engine-perf 837adbb into the copy so `coverWindow` works there; never committed), `sheets2.sh TAG TIER eng|main [rise|dive|both]` (both cover sheets, preview format), `strip2.sh TAG TIER eng|main COLS FRAMES` (stills of any frames in one browser session through `assets-src/venus/motion/frames.ts`, strip to `view/TAG.jpg`).

What the engine does (read in `src/director/film.ts`, `src/core/motion.ts`): the sky is dimmed by `(1 - coverAmount)^2`; the engine's cover pass is cut by `coverShell`; the sample count of a fast frame is scaled by `1 - coverAmount * coverHides`; a set's `near` object is drawn after a depth clear, before the engine's cover; `light.skyLow [d0, d1, level]` scales the orbit sky by `mix(level, 1, smooth(ramp(d0, d1, altitude)))` in dive and rise; the terrain sky is the mode `terrainSkyGlow 0.25`. The sky's aim changes at the swap (the engine's rule: the sky changes under a cover), so the star field jumps there in any case.

Design taken (all in my folders):
- The engine's own cover pass draws nothing: `coverShell [-2, -1]` and `coverSea` edge `[-2, -1]`. `coverAmount` is now only a small number (`veil.sky 0.02` times an eased bump), kept above 0 at the centre because the engine tests it; `coverHides 33` keeps the sample factor at 0.34 at the centre as before.
- The veil is my own pass, `veil.ts`, the set's `near`: one full screen triangle pair, rays from the camera's inverse projection (so it follows the jitter and the shutter), masked to the planet's disc (deck sphere in the terrain view, the globe in the orbit view), so it never touches the sky. Blend One, OneMinusSrcAlpha, alpha channel untouched, discarded in the diagnostic views.
- Sheets: four spheres below the camera at altitudes `lowest * step^i` (step 2.5), each with the cloud tile `veil-clouds.jpg` (from patch d, `assets-src/venus/veil/tile.py`, recipe in RECIPE.md) at a tile width of 3 sheet altitudes, the tile turned so its baked light faces the carried Sun. A sheet is born at the camera's altitude, fades in, recedes and fades out, so the pattern is the same at every altitude and streams with the true pull back. Holes from a wide noise plus the tile's luma; `amount` closes them. Sheets above 0.05 to 0.1 radii fade (`ceiling`), so the veil stays in the atmosphere when the camera is high. Lower sheets go into a fog colour that is brighter toward the Sun; at the swap a fog base closes what is left (`solid`).
- The swap is carried: `swapOf` in `set.ts` takes both poses at the swap frame. On the terrain side the sheets are seen by a virtual camera on the orbit view's sphere (turn = orbit quaternion times inverse terrain quaternion, altitude = orbit altitude at the swap times exp(rate * drop), with the rate eased in from zero at the window's edge, `veil.ease 2`). On the orbit side the real camera is used. So the sheets do not jump at the swap.
- The Sun: the terrain's painted air dome (Sun and glare) is carried into the orbit view's sky by `veil.ts` (second block, same texture, same mapping, fixed at the swap) and fades with `(1 - released)^sunFade`; the globe is graded toward the terrain picture (`look.veil.grade`, `uCarry` in `globe.ts`) and released over `veil.carry` 12 frames.
- Timing follows the window: `plan.phase()` gives -1 to 1 across `coverWindow(seg)`, 0 at the swap, so it follows `seconds` and `center`.
- Sky: `light.skyLow [0.03, 1.2, 0.55]` lowers the orbit sky toward the deck (terrain sky mode is 0.25 of the orbit sky); frames above 1.2 radii altitude do not change (1287 is at 2.63, 1586 at 4.21; dive from 1303, rise up to 1571).

Takes seen at draft (strips in `/home/user/workspace/view`, pushed as looks):
- a: noise sheets, cream. Sky, Sun carry, horizon right. Veil a pale wash.
- b: noise sheets with harder edges: flat beige blobs. Rejected; the sheets need a real cloud picture.
- c1: tile sheets, pale. Form reads as cloud banks. Too bright against the terrain (veil 177 against 40 to 130 levels), the terrain is gone 7 frames before the swap, speckle of bright tops when thin.
- c2: dark terrain colours, wide holes, eased rate, sky numbers above. Reads as a brown wrinkled surface (a third surface) and pale flat cut outs high above the globe (sheets at 0.2 radii altitude).
- c3: ceiling, fog base, translucent sheets (`dense 0.8`), Sun glow in the fog.
- c4 (first review tier strip, rise, 1552 to 1570): sky, stars, Sun and horizon continuous in every frame. But 1558 to 1562 are a flat tan wash with faint vertical streaks: the sheets zoom 1.68 times per frame at the swap (the real pull back), each sheet lives about 6 frames, the shutter averages 16 to 128 positions and at full amount every hole is closed, so only the tile's fine detail is left and it averages out. The critic's "wash with no form" again. Draft frames hide this, so the covers are judged at review tier only.
- c5 (draft, both covers, every frame): darker terrain side sheets, fog base from amount 0.55, stronger grade. Structure right, still the fast zoom.
- Decision 20:50: the sheets stream slower than the real pull back (`veil.slow`, the log of the virtual altitude is compressed about the swap on both sides; on the orbit side the ray angle from the nadir is scaled so the sheets' horizon stays on the real limb), the streak is drawn on purpose (taps along the pull back over the true shutter length, `veil.streak`, thresholded after the blur so the shapes are long and keep an edge), and holes stay open at full amount over the fog base, so there is form in every frame.

Item 5 first look (20:40, while a strip rendered): autocorrelation of the star layer in the round 23 final frame 1440, left of the frame above the limb: peak at dx 0, dy 36 (0.04). `sky-terrain.webp` has the same at dy 51 patch px (51 x 1920 / 2816 = 35 film px). The approved image has a weak one at dy 51 too (0.02). So the second copy is inside the terrain sky patch, made in `relief/air.py` (donor fill or mirror), not the shared sky and not the dome. To do: find the step and remove it.
- c6 (review, taps): the streak as 5 texture taps along the pull back per sheet, 16 times anisotropic. Looked right at 1558 (long soft streaks with light and dark groups) but cost 5.4 s per sample at preview format (a 128 sample frame 11 minutes, c4 took 1.5). Dropped.
- c7, c8 (kept design): one texture lookup per sheet. The shapes come from noise drawn in polar coordinates about the point below the camera (angle, log of distance; `look.veil.sheets.fan [12, 1.6, 2.7, 5]`, bent by the cloud noise, `wave 0.2`), mixed in by how fast the real camera pulls back (`plan.veil.rush`: log zoom over the shutter at which the streaks are full, 0.12). In those coordinates a pull back is a slide along the streak, so the streaks keep their place and their texture streams along them. `plan.veil.slow 0.45`: the sheets' virtual altitude is height at the swap times (real altitude over that height) to the power 0.45 on the orbit side, and exp(0.45 rate drop) on the terrain side, so a sheet lives about 15 frames instead of 6; on the orbit side the ray's angle from the nadir is scaled by asin(1/(1+low)) / asin(1/(1+high)) so the sheets end on the real limb. Holes stay open at full amount (`thin 0.9`, linear `ramp 1`) over the fog base (`solid [0.55, 1]`), so no frame is a flat wash. The streaks are in the draft tier too, so draft strips show the veil as it is.
- Window: 1.0 s for both covers (plan `coverWindow`), frames 1299 to 1328 and 1545 to 1574. With 0.8 s the terrain thinned over 6 frames, with 1.0 s over 8 (1549 to 1556) and the globe comes over 8 (1564 to 1571). `skyLow [0.03, 2, 0.55]`: the orbit sky rises from 0.55 to 1 between 0.03 and 2 radii of altitude (frames 1291 to 1314 and 1560 to 1574; 1287 at 2.63 and 1586 at 4.21 are not touched).

### State 17:30, the orange red tints of the place cured by code (item 3 of the list sent with 8b65c470)

No new mail from /root since mail 295. Standing order: work on the own list, name a commit when a cure is rendered and proven.

Cause, measured:

- No plate holds the red: in display values the red over green of plate a at its 99th percentile is 1.37. The red came from two steps of the drawing.
- First, the plates are drawn dimmer than they are held (`uPlaceDusk`, the dusk of the globe side). The dimming acted on the light, the display value taken back through the film curve. The light of a highlight that the curve pressed has far more colour than the picture shows: display 235, 190, 130 is light 1.14, 0.37, 0.15. Dimmed, that turned the lit sides of the towers orange red.
- Second, the tone map (`place3-tone-<kind>.bin`) raised each channel to the power and multiplied it by the factor on its own: red and green speckles in the pale fan, red towers beside it.

Cure, by code, no new take:

- `globe.ts`: `uPlaceDusk` is a vec4. By its share `.w` the colour is that of the display value at the luminance of the light, applied right after the light is read. The power of the tone map acts on the luminance (`toneLum`), and of the plate's own colour the share `1 - tone.colour` is kept inside `tone.edge` (`uToneColour`).
- `set.ts`: `.w = clamp(dusk.hue * (1 - luminance of placeDusk), 0, 1)`, so at the handover, where the plates are not dimmed, they show as they are.
- `plates.json`: `tone.colour` 0.8, `dusk.hue` 1.0 with a note each. `assets.ts` reads them.
- `tlay.py tone` made again for both kinds with the same formula (power 0.631 to 2.604, factor dive 0.048 to 238.955, rise 0.046 to 238.955), the four bins under `public/assets/venus/{full,web}/` written again. `RECIPE.md` tells both steps.

Measured on nine test frames at draft, share of the frame with red over 1.7 times green and red over 90, before and after: 1282 0.41 to 0.22 percent, 1287 0.48 to 0.17, 1292 0.43 to 0.12, 1298 0.24 to 0.08, 1304 0.05 to 0.03, 1568 0.01 to 0.00, 1574 0.20 to 0.00, 1580 0.38 to 0.06, 1586 0.30 to 0.11. Tried and dropped: the power on the luminance alone (no change), `tone.colour` 0.8 alone (1287 0.43), `dusk.hue` 2.0 (about the same as 1.0).

## Mail from handover_engineer on plan E (22:50 UTC, word for word)

"handover_engineer to venus_builder: plan E (the Builder's MAIL 369 e: E is the engine's one move and the default for all nine; d148 let you fly your own path, now a stop keeps one only for a need it shows me).
WHAT IT IS. In a dive and a rise the film's camera is the engine's, in both views: one glide over the whole segment between your two ends. Far end: hold(time - hold.start) going on (rise: after(time), the pose the travel leaves from). Near end: the first pose of your surface view, terrain(0), through your twin, carried back at its own velocity as a straight line (rise: the last pose carried on), reach at most handover.coastFrames (8) frames. One share for the log of the height, the direction about the place, the attitude and the field of view; its rate is one bell (flanks 0.4 and 0.4 of the segment, corners eased), zero at both seams, so the move meets the hold and the surface view at their own speed and direction. The close view is the same eye through the inverse of your twin. T (`at`) only says which view draws.
A STOP STILL SETS: hold(), terrain(), twin(), turn(), spin(); handover.dive.at, rise.at; path.sidestep, path.level, path.levelBy; path.rise and path.fall (the bell's flank shares of the whole segment; refused when the step of the rate would pass smooth.path.maxStep).
THE ENGINE IGNORES on E: your overrides of divePose, risePose, dive, rise (steadyHeight, above, limb, slope): the film calls plan.eye(kind, time, view) of the engine, which a stop may not override (a test asserts it); terrain.entry* and exit*; path.turnRise, turnFall, fromDive.
READ INSTEAD OF A CLOCK: plan.eyeHeight(time), the film's eye above the unit sphere in radii. Your placeLook, phase, veilAmount, drop, release, skyGain and coverAmount hang on your own path's time today; on E (and for plan F) they take eyeHeight.
HOW IT LANDS: my block of the config gets `handover.ownPath`, the list of stops still on their own path; in my first commit (due 00:45 UTC) every stop but Mars, so your bytes do not change when it goes onto main. `--diag onemove` draws any stop on E without touching the list. You go onto E by deleting "venus" from that list in a commit of your own (that one edit in my block is yours) and dropping the overrides.
VENUS. The `at` that keeps your present height at T (0.0208 and 0.0184 radii): dive 0.927 (T in 1343, as now), rise 0.124 (T in 1539, now 1542). The harness reads your worst step now as 0.164 and 0.214 of the mean (limit 0.08). If the steady path through the deck needs something the two ends, the place, at, sidestep, level and the flanks cannot give, write me the need in two lines; a stop that stays on the list is bound by npm run smooth at whole and half frames and across both seams all the same."

globe_engineer: "globe_engineer to venus_builder, the cap and the air in short. State: code written on agent/engine-globe, not pushed yet (unit tests green, pictures not made yet); I send you the commit when the first pictures of the synthetic height hold. It goes onto main only after /root proves it. Read with that in mind: Venus does not use src/bodies/planet.ts today (only HAZE_GLSL), and the cap as built hangs on Planet.

1. THE CAP (src/bodies/cap.ts, class ReliefCap, option `cap` of Planet). A stop hands: height levels coarse to fine, each a square gnomonic plate about the spot of its patches (north up, row 0 north, texel centres at (i + 0.5) / N), raw uint16, height in radii = low + v / 65535 * (high - low), with widthDeg and size per level; kept on the card as 16 bit integers (sets.ts heightTexture(ctx, data, size), counted in the set's bytes, 10.7 MB for 2048 squared with its mips). Also border [inner, outer] in radii (the height goes to 0 there), from [high, low] (heights of the eye between which the relief grows from 0 to full, over the log of height), cells per level side, and the pixel as an angle. It draws: a displaced mesh (instanced patches on one lattice per level, vertices on texel centres, level of the heights chosen by the pixel's footprint), in the same depth buffer as the sphere, with the globe's own fragment text and the globe's own uniforms, so colour, light, haze and levels are the globe's: the colour is read at the undisplaced direction (lay it as a map from straight above). Real parallax and self occlusion. Not there: no cast shadows, no normal from the heights yet (the light is the globe's), haze depth still measured to the sphere, no fragment march yet. A cloud deck with towers 0.002 to 0.004 radii at an eye never under 0.016 is well inside what it is made for. For a globe that is not a Planet the vertex text (capVert) and ReliefCap take any fragment text that reads vLocal, vWorldN, vPos, vView, vClip, plus the uniforms uSpotN, uSpotE, uSpotU, uSpin; the sphere under it needs one discard line (uCapCut). Tell me which globe program Venus draws with and I say what it takes.

2. THE AIR is not a new volume: it is the same haze as today (HAZE_GLSL: depth, scale height, day, twilight, night, edge, strength, extinction, forward), but its numbers come as one curve over the log of the eye's height instead of by view or by time. The stop gives knots in its params (`air: [{ height, ...fields }, ...]`, highest first), the film (handover_engineer, type in src/core/types.ts) mixes them and hands shot.air per sample; in src/bodies/air.ts setHazeAir(uniforms, air.haze) writes them into any material that includes HAZE_GLSL and made its uniforms with hazeUniforms, so both views of a stop can call it if both include HAZE_GLSL. A true volume by height with a phase function is not in this task; if Venus needs one say what it must do that HAZE_GLSL cannot and I take it to /root as its own option.

3. Branch agent/engine-globe; the commit follows by message, on main when /root has proven it."

Decision: the globe side at T has to be the surface view's own scene, not a picture of it. `relief.ts` draws the meshes of the surface view and its air under the horizon on the globe side too ("the ground on the globe side", `globeGround`, `updateGround`): same geometry, same textures, a second program whose eye is given, hung in the globe's scene by the similarity of the plan (group turned by the twin's turn, scale 1 / radius, deck centre on the globe's centre). Depth on its own logarithmic scale in the near half of the buffer, so the layers hide one another and the globe's sphere, which runs through the towers, cuts none of them. ## NOTE 501 from the Builder, 03:38 UTC (word for word)

NOTE 501 to every stop builder and globe_engineer, from the Builder, 03:38 UTC. A fault of the whole film, found by the first whole smooth report from the machines (Mercury, job 14): the same film frame at uhd is not the same picture as at 16 by 9 (one block differs by 45.8 levels at 713, limit 12).
CAUSE, found by mercury_builder: every globe brings its plate levels and its fine levels in by the texels of the parent a pixel of the format (uPatchFade 1.1 to 1.7 against gd * scale * size, gd from dFdx and dFdy). At uhd a pixel is half as large, so every level comes in at twice the height; at preview at half the height; in the live player it depends on the window. Brandon captures at uhd, so he gets another film than the one we judge. The term is in src/bodies/planet.ts (globe_engineer) and in the own globe code of mercury, venus, earth, jupiter, uranus, neptune and the Sun (src/stops/<stop>/globe.ts or planet.ts).
RULING (plan F: whatever blends does so by distance, height or angle): the measure is texels of the parent a 1080th of the frame height, an angle, not a pixel. In practice one factor, the height of the drawing buffer in pixels over 1080 (1 at 16 by 9, 2 at uhd, 0.5 at preview), multiplied into the density that a fade reads (parent, texels, fine, thin, cap, whatever your code calls it) and into nothing that only picks a mip for sampling.
PROOF, both by you before you name the commit: (a) at 16 by 9 the factor is 1 and every byte stays: the hashes of your own draft frames before and after are equal. (b) at uhd the picture becomes the 16 by 9 picture, only finer: npm run smooth -- --stop ID --only parity on your tree (seven frames), limits mean 12, coarse mean 3.2, one block 12, frame level 2.2.
THE SAME RULE holds for every other number in your stop that is counted in pixels and can be seen: the width of a feather, the radius of a glow, a threshold of a size on screen, a point size. If your parity is still red with the factor in, the panel names the block: find the term.
WHO: each stop builder, in the commit you name next (mercury_builder has it in work). globe_engineer: src/bodies/planet.ts and anything else under src/bodies and src/core that reads a density a pixel, as one commit on newest main (6884e80 or later), then ask me for the engine proof and say which stops draw with the shared code. saturn_coder and mars_place_builder: check your place code for the same kind of term and say what you found.
A red parity is a severe item in a stop's round.

## NOTE 504 from the Builder, 03:51 UTC (word for word)

NOTE 504 to every stop builder, from the Builder, 03:51 UTC. On NOTE 501 (the factor), two things from globe_engineer that save you a wrong factor:
1. Do NOT take the factor from view.format in the pass that draws a place picture. There view.format is the layout's, larger by the picture's scale (2 at 16 by 9), so view.format.height over 1080 is 2 at 16 by 9 in that pass and your place picture's bytes change. And the edge limit (handover.place.maxEdge 4800) gives the uhd picture the scale 1, so a pixel of the uhd place picture is a pixel of the master's place picture: there the right factor at uhd is 1, not 2, for code that does not already multiply by uFine. Code that multiplies its density by uFine (the terrain shaders) needs the format's factor alone.
2. The shared helper, in proof now and on main as soon as it is clean (agent/engine-globe, globe_engineer names the commit): src/core/frame.ts with frameUniform (the format's height over the master's, set by the engine in applySize, usable as a uniform), setPass (the engine sets it while a place picture is drawn) and bufferFrame() (the two multiplied, for code that reads a density a pixel of the buffer and knows nothing of uFine).
RULING: use the helper, not a factor of your own. If your cure is already written with your own uniform (uranus_builder: seen.ts), keep working with it and swap its source to the helper when I tell you it is on main; that swap changes no byte and needs no new proof beyond the hashes. If you have not started, fetch globe_engineer's commit when it names it and write against the helper. Stops with no place picture left (plan F) have only case 1's last sentence to mind.

## MAIL 526 from the Builder (/root), 04:52 UTC, word for word

MAIL 526 from the Builder (/root), 04:52 UTC, one mail to every stop builder and to handover_engineer: THE SEAM WITH THE SURFACE VIEW. A ruling (d196).

FOUND on Mars's rise at 60 pictures a second. MEASURED by me on the pictures: the change from picture to picture falls from 5.3 to 2.7 within three capture frames after the seam (film frame 2670) and is at 8.8 four later. The cause, measured by handover_engineer on the path (STATED): the eye's own speed over its own height falls to 0.33 of the surface view's at 2671 + 1/2 and is at 2.2 five capture frames later. The surface view pushes toward its place; the rise pulls back along the line from the place to the eye; so the eye stops and turns back. The path part of `npm run smooth` is green over it, because it reads the picture's speed round the place and not the eye against the near ground. This is a "moment of lag" at the change of view, and it is in the film, not in the player.

THE RULE. Plan E says a dive and a rise meet "the surface view's own move with the same speed and direction". That holds for the frames after the seam as well as at it: across each seam with the surface view the eye's speed over its own height never dips and never turns back. A new line in the path part of `npm run smooth` will read it at all 17 seams (harness_builder, due 05:40 UTC). Its limit is set from a calibration on main and logged before any round uses it.

WHERE IT IS CURED: in the surface view's own path, which is yours. Not in the engine's law: handover_engineer searched the law four times, and every cure there turns the lens more than the turn limit allows in the frames a rise has. STATED by handover_engineer, a scratch on Mars with the surface view's velocity at the seam turned: pulling back up its own line, the rise's lowest speed is 1.05 and it never turns back; across its lens 0.95 and 1.02; 45 degrees off 0.53; pushing at its place 0.33. A dive arrives down the surface view's way (0.98 and more on the one move).

So a surface view is one flight that takes the dive's motion at its first frame and hands the rise its motion at its last. Where yours pushes in, it bends over its last seconds from the push into a track across and on into the pull back, without losing speed (no rest: a rest is a dent of its own) and with the lens turning inside the turn limits. Where yours already pulls back or tracks across at its end, show it with the new line and change nothing.

WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE: the picture of the judged surface frame. On a finished stop its camera stays to the byte (Sun 0, 60 and 90, Mars 2580, Jupiter 3150, Saturn 3720); on the others the composition of the approved close image at the judged frame stands. The bend lives after the judged frame. On Mars, whose surface view Brandon approved in motion, nothing before frame 2610 changes.

WHO, by handover_engineer's numbers (the eye's lowest speed over the surface view's own, on your own path today unless it says forced): Mars 0.33 (rise), Uranus 0.46 at 4382 (rise), Earth 0.64 at 2116 (rise) and 0.69 at 1905 (dive), Venus 0.78 (dive), Mercury 0.83 at 961 (rise), Sun 0.92 (0.38 forced onto the one move), Jupiter 0.76 forced (its view is nearly still at the seam), Neptune 0.98, Saturn not measured. On Mars the bend goes into mars_place_builder's commit; handover_engineer gives it the numbers.

TIME. The 07:00 UTC point of d186 stands for everything else. A stop that needs this bend may have until 08:30 UTC for its NAMED mail if it tells me so in one line before 07:00 with what is done and what is left. I mail the sha of the new line as soon as it is on main; until then the engineer's scratch is the guide.

No answer is needed unless you ask for the later time or see a reason the rule cannot hold on your stop; then say which frame and why.

## MAIL 596 from the Builder (/root), about 09:04 UTC, word for word

MAIL 596 from the Builder (/root) to the nine stop builders. A check tool for the pattern number is on main 81d568a7 (globe_engineer's NAMED f65859e1): `assets-src/shared/globe-levels.py`. It lays one level of a plate pyramid against the part of its parent that it covers, both at the state in which the level comes in (a parent texel 0.8 px of the frame), and judges the pair with the smooth report's own `pattern` function and the config's numbers. Seconds, no render. Merge main, or copy that one file to the same path in your tree, then:
python3 assets-src/shared/globe-levels.py --dir public/assets/ID/full --json src/stops/ID/FILE.json [--key levels] [--suffix=-dive] [--pairs 0-1,1-3] [--panel out.png]
or with the levels by hand: --level FILE:WIDTHDEG[:EASTDEG,NORTHDEG] twice or more (a plate given by the tangent of its half width: WIDTHDEG = 2 atan of it). One line a pair, OVER and exit 1 above smooth.pictures.maxPattern. It reads files, not the shader: a pair is a test only when both files are the same kind of picture (colour with colour, light with light), and it knows nothing of what a stop does with a level by height.

MEASURED by me on main's Mars (the old plates): 0.06, 0.00, 0.06, 0.00, 0.00, 0.00, 0.00 in 3.5 s, as its author states. MEASURED by globe_engineer on the proof trees of the first named commits (not checked by me), 99th percentile against 0.45:
- Mars b83618ec: patch-19 to land-8p5 1.19 OVER, land-3p8 to land-1p6 0.69 OVER, land-1p6 to land-0p7 0.59 OVER, land-0p7 to land-0p3 0.98 OVER; the other three pairs 0.00 to 0.09. In the panel of the first pair the parent shows a bright mound with a crater where the child shows a dark plain with the canyon crack.
- Mercury 9b5f55cd: patch-1 to patch-2 1.09 OVER (dive), patch-2 to patch-3r 0.70 OVER (rise), the others 0.01 to 0.02.
- Uranus 9a369939: every pair 0.00 to 0.01. Its red is not in the plates.
- Venus 3b52b0eb: colour 0.01 and 0.02; light a to b 0.20 and 0.13; light b to d 1.12 and 1.10 OVER, with a caution (the two light plates may not be the same quantity).
- Not run: Saturn, Jupiter, Earth, Neptune, the Sun.

RULED. Where a pair is over, two levels show two different pictures of the same ground, the red pattern number of that move is true, and no exchange by height, however slow, cures it (plan F: one place). The cure is in the files: a level is made from the level under it, or both from one source, so that reduced to its parent's scale it is its parent. Where every pair is clean and the move is still red, the cause is in what the shader adds by height or angle (a second look mixed in, a function layer, a light term), and the same rule holds there: one ground, one law of light, borders set on the ground. No limit moves.

Asked of each of you: run it now on every pyramid your dive and rise show (both sets where they differ) and put its lines into your next NAMED mail. A pair over the limit is named there as red, with its cure. This changes no due time.

## The glow of the limb laid on the ground (trial H, 12:59 on)

| frame | samples | raw px over the full shutter | share of the shutter kept | px open | px between samples | taps of the stop |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1280 | 64 | 20.2 | 0.692 | 14.0 | 0.22 | 0 |
| 1287 | 64 | 36.5 | 0.500 | 18.3 | 0.29 | 0 |
| 1292 | 64 | 53.8 | 0.500 | 26.9 | 0.42 | 0 |
| 1304 | 64 | 74.9 | 0.500 | 37.4 | 0.58 | 0 |

  The cap of the blur (`handover.maxBlurPx` 14) is not reached where the share stands on its floor (`handover.minShutter` 0.5): 18 to 38 px stay open.
- Separate copies: the samples are 0.29 px apart at 1287, and the stop's own taps inside a sample are 0 at the review and final tiers (they start over 1 px a sample). The spectrum of the final still over the spectrum of the closed one, in four crops of 384 px, falls along one direction to a first zero at 1 / 8.0, 1 / 14.2, 1 / 7.5 and 1 / 9.6 px (the length of a box) and stays low beyond it (mean 0.16 to 0.27 above 0.1 cycles per px, no return to 1). So there are no copies of one edge: each bright pebble (6 to 10 px wide) is drawn out into a bar of 8 to 14 px with hard ends, and a row of pebbles reads as a row of copies. Across the motion the ratio is 0.57 to 1.28: nothing is lost that way.

- Why it reads as stretch and not as blur ("stars and the limb stay sharp"): `src/core/engine.ts` draws the sky of every sample with the pose of the middle of the frame (`this.sky.render(..., mid.skyQuaternion, ...)` with `cam.fov = mid.camera.vfov`), so no star is drawn out, while by the film's own cameras a star on the axis moves 13.4 px over the open shutter at 1287 (14.9 at 1292, 13.9 at 1304, 11.8 at 1570, 11.1 at 1586; `out/work/venus/place/fsky.ts`). The centre of the body moves 6.0 px and its radius grows 7.0 px in the same time, the surface up to 18.3 px.

So the cause is not in the stop: it is the shutter of the engine (a box of 18 to 38 px over a field of pebbles 6 to 10 px wide, its floor over its cap) and the sky that the engine draws without the move. ### The share that left 0 to 1 (MAIL 754, point 2)

- Seen again here (out/work/venus/place/fcarry.ts, every eighth of a frame of the dive and the rise, 1320 instants): 1 outside 0 to 1, "dive 1266 + 0.375 carry -1.1102230246251565e-15"; the low share never.
- Cause: `below` (plan.ts) is 1 less the curve of the share of the way between two heights. The curve of the carry is the quintic `smoother` of path.ts, t * t * t * (t * (t * 6 - 15) + 10) with t held to 0 to 1. Just under the upper height of sky.carry (3.4 radii) t is a little under 1 and the polynomial comes out 1 + 1.1e-15 by rounding, so the share is minus 1.1e-15. No real overshoot: the curve cannot leave 0 to 1 but by rounding.
- Cure: `below` holds what the curve gives to 0 to 1, in the one place where every share by height of the stop is made (the two sky shares, the dusk, and the weights of set.ts). `smoother` itself is not touched: the path of the dive and the rise reads it, and the cameras stay to the byte.
- Test: `tests/venus-shares.test.ts` asks the instant (the share itself and `FilmDirector.shotAt(1266, (1266 + 0.375) / fps, 'orbit')`, the call that threw) and every eighth of a frame of the dive and the rise. DECISION, said in the mail: the test is one new file OUTSIDE my three folders, because vitest only reads `tests/**/*.test.ts` (vite.config.ts) and MAIL 754 orders a unit test. Nothing else outside the folders is touched.

## MAIL 785 from the Builder (/root), 22:45 UTC, word for word

One ruling for every stop, for your awareness and your next commit. It changes no due time.
Four builders (Neptune, Sun, Jupiter, Earth) read their dives and rises frame by frame tonight and each found the same cause behind what Brandon's third note calls an image that pops up, a flat smudge that turns into the canyon and a moment where things load in: two pictures of one ground weighed against each other by the camera's height, or a region that takes another look by a share of the height. So: nothing is cured by such a weight. A stop has one ground at every height; what the surface view needs at the place is a permanent thing of the planet at its true size, drawn by one law; detail comes by distance (the size of a pixel on the ground), haze and tone by the length of the path through the air. Where that thing is in view at the hold, the hold may change inside a small disc round the place and keeps its bytes outside it; the hold beside the approved hero at 1 to 1 comes to me before such a commit is named.
Allowed, and not meant by this: a grade that follows the camera's height slowly through the whole move, as an eye adapts, if no frame shows it as a thing arriving (the pattern line green, and by eye). Not allowed: a picture, a layer or a region that comes in or goes out by height.
Answer in two lines, with your next mail and not before: which laws of your stop still weigh two pictures or two looks by height, at which frames they show, and whether your commit in hand removes them.

### MAIL 802, the work: screen pixel terms through the frame factor, texels counted in the full set (23:38 to 23:58 UTC)

Audit of the stop's source for terms that count screen pixels or texels of the loaded set. Already through the frame factor: the fades of patches and of the place (`parent * uFrame`), the threshold and the smear of the motion (`bufferFrame()`). Free of the size by construction: relief `perHeight`, `closeScale`, levels given in degrees times the loaded width. Not through it, cured in this commit: the limb's edge in pixels (set.ts, `LIMB.edgePx * frameScale / radiusPx`), the presence of the globe by its radius in pixels (`radiusPx / frameScale > 0.6`), the veil's edge in pixels (veil.ts, `edgePx * bufferFrame()`), the count of motion taps (`px / scale / look.motion.step`). Counting the loaded set's texels, cured in this commit: the exchange of the globe's map for patches and of patches for plates (globe.ts: `texels * uMapPerFull`, `gd * uPatchScale * uPatchFull`, `pgd * uPlaceScale * uPlaceFull`), the mip levels of the place's forms (lowered by log2 of full over loaded), the level of the relief's matte (relief.ts, `levelsUnderFull`). The full set's widths are written in plates.json (`texels`), wrap.json and relief.json; loading the full set throws if a picture has another width than written.

Measured, draft tier, mean absolute difference of the two pictures of a pair, 0 to 255, the 3840 wide one reduced by 2 where sizes are compared. Before the cure, frame 1299: sets at 1920 wide 1.254, sets at 3840 wide 1.475, sizes in the full set 1.581, sizes in the web set 1.555; frame 1323: 1.111, 1.041, 1.351, 1.325. After the cure, frame 1299: 0.990, 1.241, 1.580, 1.501; frame 1323: 1.303, 1.246, 1.351, 1.288. Means of 24 px blocks, sets at 1920 wide: 1299 mean 0.401 and largest 11.48 before, 0.229 and 2.88 after; 1323 mean 0.369 and largest 7.09 before, 0.330 and 5.10 after. By eye before the cure the web set at 1323 showed a mosaic of cells and an orange streak where it had exchanged levels earlier than the full set; after it the sets differ in fine forms only (web softer), no mosaic, no moved border.

What is left between the sizes, measured in the full set with the engine's grain off: 1299 mean 0.935 (1.580 with grain), 1323 mean 0.679 (1.351 with grain). Without the engine's grade and post chain (diag ungraded), 1299: mean 0.774, means of 24 px blocks 0.201 and largest 6.71 at x 1128, y 144, which by eye is the bright limb and the fine forms next to it, the same forms and the same borders, finer at 3840 wide. The sky past the bright limb at x 20, y 0 to 80 of 1299 reads red 11.40 at 1920 wide against 4.84 at 3840 wide with the post chain, and 3.20 against 3.19 without it: the wider glow at 1920 wide is made in the engine's post chain (src/post/chain.ts, bloom over a fixed count of halvings of the buffer), outside this stop's folders.   - `plates.json` air.field: degrees [13, 22] from the foot of the camera of T at the centre of the body, and top 0.35. `assets.ts` gives them as `place.air.field` (radians) and `place.air.top`.
  - The dome (`relief.ts`, `airField` in the globe side's air shader): each line of sight takes the field at its ground point, or at the limb point under it where it passes over the limb. So the air stands whole over its place from the limb upward. The air under the limb (`globeUnder`) keeps field 1; it goes by ground.bandHeights as before.
  - The haze of the ground (`globe.ts`, uniform `uAirField`): the field at the ground point, times the law by the line of sight (e to the minus cosine over haze.mu), less its value at the cosine `top` and stretched to 1 again. ### Point 4, the footprint at grazing sight: measured by rays (19:24 UTC)

- /tmp/v/foot.py: for a pixel of the master frame, the camera of the frame (out/work/venus/place/geo11.ts), rays through the pixel onto the deck (sphere of radius 1), the image of the pixel's circle on the deck (the two axes of the map from the screen to the deck); beside it the eye's formula of globe.ts (step 2) and the screen's two derivatives as a sampler reads them (the longer one is the long axis, taps = the ratio of the two lengths rounded up, blur across = the longer over the taps).
- Frame 1555 + 1/2 (eye r 1.08665, vfov 54.97), five pixels at 6.4 to 13.2 deg of sight over the deck (1582, 226; 1550, 215; 1443, 193; 1500, 250; 1600, 300): the eye's formula over the rays 1.01 to 1.03 along the line of sight and 0.97 to 0.99 across. The screen's reading across the line of sight over the rays: 2.64, 2.54, 1.89, 1.38, 1.32. At 1582, 226: rays 0.1194 by 0.0140 deg (ratio 8.5), formula 0.1219 by 0.0137, screen 0.1108 by 0.0466 read as 3 taps, 0.0369 across.
- Frame 1563 + 1/2 (eye r 1.22503, vfov 50.09), four pixels at 15.3 to 27.1 deg (1532, 180; 1632, 230; 1700, 300; 1500, 300): the formula over the rays 1.04 to 1.06 along and 0.94 to 0.96 across. The screen's reading across over the rays: 1.21, 1.32, 1.23, 0.85.
- CAUSE of what was open at 18:35 ("why the formula reads less there I have not found"): the screen's two derivatives are two conjugate diameters of the footprint's ellipse, not its axes. Where the line of sight on the deck does not lie along a screen axis, both derivatives hold a share of the long axis; a sampler that takes the longer one as the axis and the ratio of the two lengths as the anisotropy sees a ratio of 2.4 where the footprint's is 8.5, and blurs across the line of sight by up to 2.6 times too much. That is why the plates' cells were softer on the far ground with the screen's footprint (control cF2) and why its row read 0.27 against 0.48.
- ANSWER, DECIDED: the eye's footprint (step 2) is the true one at grazing sight, within 2 to 6 percent of the rays at the nine pixels measured. It stays. The row 1555 + 1/2 (0.48) is then the reading of fine cells of the far deck that the true footprint shows; its cure is not a wider filter.

### Cure B, written 20:50 to 20:55 UTC, not yet rendered: one exchange at a pixel

- Read in globe.ts: the picture of the globe at a pixel is R(a) * (1 - c * a) + seen * c * a, with R(a) the hold's picture with the wide ring at its share, seen the plates, c their cover, a = arrive at the ground point. The ground of H1 over it with alpha a * body leaves a * (1 - a) * body * c * (seen - R) too much of the flat plates inside the ground: the second tower. Two layers of the ground over one another at the share a each leave the same kind of excess between them (the tower group over the ground it stands on).
- The cure: the close side is one picture, the ground over its plates. In a move the globe lays the plates whole wherever any of them has come (globe.ts, uOver 1: the mix by c in place of c * a), the ground stands whole on them (relief.ts as on the branch, no share of its own, no height: set.ts weight 1 in both moves), and a second mesh of the globe (Globe.over, the same sphere, the same shader and uniforms, uOver 2, drawn last, no depth test) draws R(a) with the air and the gain over the whole with alpha 1 - a. Where no ground stands the sum is (1 - a) * R + a * (R * (1 - c) + seen * c), the same as now. Where it stands it is (1 - a) * R + a * (the ground over the plates): one carrier of the close picture, one exchange. The air (a mix by a weight of the pixel) and the gain act the same on both, so the sum under them is the sum.
- What it costs: the globe's shader runs twice on the disc in both moves where a is under 1 (the second time without the plates); one more program, made in the hold by a dry draw as the ground's are (relief.ts, dryable, now exported), so the hold draws one more sphere into an empty box. The air under the horizon (the under dome, by bandHeights, low heights only) comes under the hold's share as the rest of the close side does.
- The straight line: relief.ts, the wide margin (aroundT) times the same ramp inside the outline as the border has (smoothstep of inside over uMatte.x), so nothing of the ground stands where its meshes end. No new number.
- Out of a move uOver is 0 and the mesh over is dry: the hold's three draft stills must stay byte equal (to check first).
